title: Effort Matters
simplified_paragraphs: 唐朝大诗人李白小时候不喜欢学习，常常不去上课，到街上玩。
一天，李白又没有去上学，在街上东看看、西看看，温暖的阳光、快乐的小鸟、美丽的花草，天气太好了！“这么好的天气，如果一天都在房间里学习多没意思！”
在一个小房子门口，坐着一个老婆婆，正在磨非常粗的铁棒。李白走过去，“老婆婆，您在做什么？”“我要把这个铁棒磨成一根针。”老婆婆回答李白。“针？”李白又问：“是做衣服的针吗？”“当然！”
“可是，铁棒这么粗，什么时候可以呢？”
老婆婆问李白：“水滴可以穿透石头，铁棒为什么不能呢？只要我比别人努力，就会成功。
老婆婆的话，让李白很不好意思，回去以后，再也没有不去学校，学习也特别努力，成了非常有名的大诗人。
“只要功夫深，铁杵磨成针。”千年过去，中国人还是非常喜爱这句话。
traditional_paragraphs: 唐朝大詩人李白小時候不喜歡學習，常常不去上課，到街上玩。
一天，李白又沒有去上學，在街上東看看、西看看，溫暖的陽光、快樂的小鳥、美麗的花草，天氣太好了！“這麼好的天氣，如果一天都在房間裡學習多沒意思！”
在一個小房子門口，坐著一個老婆婆，正在磨非常粗的鐵棒。李白走過去，“老婆婆，您在做什麼？”“我要把這個鐵棒磨成一根針。”老婆婆回答李白。“針？”李白又問：“是做衣服的針嗎？”“當然！”
“可是，鐵棒這麼粗，什麼時候可以呢？”
老婆婆問李白：“水滴可以穿透石頭，鐵棒為什麼不能呢？只要我比別人努力，就會成功。
老婆婆的話，讓李白很不好意思，回去以後，再也沒有不去學校，學習也特別努力，成了非常有名的大詩人。
“只要功夫深，鐵杵磨成針。”千年過去，中國人還是非常喜愛這句話。
pinyin_paragraphs: Táng cháo dà shī rén Lǐ Bái xiǎo shí hou bù xǐ huan xué xí， cháng cháng bù qù shàng kè， dào jiē shang wán。

yī tiān， Lǐ Bái yòu méi yǒu qù shàng xué， zài jiē shang dōng kàn kàn、 xī kàn kàn， wēn nuǎn de yáng guāng、 kuài lè de xiǎo niǎo、 měi lì de huā cǎo， tiān qì tài hǎo le！“ zhè me hǎo de tiān qì， rú guǒ yī tiān dōu zài fáng jiān lǐ xué xí duō méi yì si！”

zài yī gè xiǎo fáng zi mén kǒu， zuò zhe yī gè lǎo pó pó， zhèng zài mó fēi cháng cū de tiě bàng。 Lǐ Bái zǒu guò qù，“ lǎo pó pó， nín zài zuò shén me？”“ wǒ yào bǎ zhè ge tiě bàng mó chéng yī gēn zhēn。” lǎo pó pó huí dá Lǐ Bái。“ zhēn？” Lǐ Bái yòu wèn：“ shì zuò yī fu de zhēn ma？”“ dāng rán！”
“ kě shì， tiě bàng zhè me cū， shén me shí hou kě yǐ ne？”
lǎo pó pó wèn Lǐ Bái：“ shuǐ dī kě yǐ chuān tòu shí tou， tiě bàng wèi shén me bù néng ne？ zhǐ yào wǒ bǐ bié rén nǔ lì， jiù huì chéng gōng。
lǎo pó pó de huà， ràng Lǐ Bái hěn bù hǎo yì si， huí qù yǐ hòu， zài yě méi yǒu bù qù xué xiào， xué xí yě tè bié nǔ lì， chéng le fēi cháng yǒu míng de dà shī rén。
“ zhǐ yào gōng fu shēn， tiě chǔ mó chéng zhēn。” qiān nián guò qù， Zhōng guó rén hái shi fēi cháng xǐ ài zhè jù huà。
english_paragraphs: When the great Tang dynasty poet Li Bai was young, he did not like studying. He often skipped class and went to play in the streets.

One day, Li Bai skipped school again. As he wandered through the streets, he looked around at the warm sunshine, the cheerful birds, and the beautiful flowers and plants. The weather was wonderful! “What a waste it would be to spend such a lovely day indoors studying!” he thought.

Outside a small house sat an old woman, grinding away at a very thick iron rod. Li Bai walked over. “What are you doing, ma’am?” he asked. “I’m grinding this iron rod into a needle,” she replied. “A needle?” Li Bai asked. “You mean a needle for sewing clothes?” “Of course!”
“But the iron rod is so thick. How long will that take?”
The old woman asked Li Bai, “If drops of water can wear through stone, why can’t I grind an iron rod into a needle? As long as I keep working hard, I’ll succeed.”
The old woman’s words made Li Bai feel ashamed. After he went home, he never skipped school again. He studied especially hard and became a very famous poet.
“With enough perseverance, an iron rod can be ground into a needle.” A thousand years have passed, but people in China still cherish this saying.

One day, Li Bai skipped school again. As he wandered through the streets, he looked around at the warm sunshine, the cheerful birds, and the beautiful flowers and plants. The weather was wonderful! “What a waste it would be to spend such a lovely day indoors studying!” he thought.

Outside a small house sat an old woman, grinding away at a very thick iron rod. Li Bai walked over. “What are you doing, ma’am?” he asked. “I’m grinding this iron rod into a needle,” she replied. “A needle?” Li Bai asked. “You mean a needle for sewing clothes?” “Of course!”

“But the iron rod is so thick. How long will that take?”

The old woman asked Li Bai, “If drops of water can wear through stone, why can’t I grind an iron rod into a needle? As long as I keep working hard, I’ll succeed.”

The old woman’s words made Li Bai feel ashamed. After he went home, he never skipped school again. He studied especially hard and became a very famous poet.

“With enough perseverance, an iron rod can be ground into a needle.” A thousand years have passed, but people in China still cherish this saying.
